stem:

modelAnswer:

stem:
If A(-2, 6) and B(7, -3), find the slope of line:
(i) parallel to AB.
(ii) perpendicular to AB.
keyPoints: ["Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals"]
modelAnswer:
$m_{AB}=\frac{-3-6}{7+2}=\frac{-9}{9}=-1$.
i. Parallel slope: $-1$. ii. Perpendicular slope: $1$.

stem: Find $x$ if the slope of line passing through $\mathrm{A}(3, x), \mathrm{B}(5,8)$ is 4.
keyPoints: ["Set the given gradient equal to rise over run"]

stem: Find k if lines passing through $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{k}, 2), \mathrm{B}(3,5)$ and $\mathrm{C}(5,-1), \mathrm{D}(8,7)$ are parallel.
keyPoints: ["Equal gradients characterise parallel lines"]
modelAnswer:
Parallel lines have equal gradients.
$m_{AB}=\frac{5-2}{3-k}=\frac{3}{3-k}$ and $m_{CD}=\frac{7+1}{8-5}=\frac{8}{3}$.
Equating: $\frac{3}{3-k}=\frac{8}{3}$ gives $9=24-8k$, so $k=\frac{15}{8}$.

stem: Find k if lines passing through $\mathrm{P}(-1,2), \mathrm{Q}(4,7)$ and $\mathrm{R}(2, \mathrm{k}), \mathrm{S}(7,10)$ are perpendicular.
keyPoints: ["Product of perpendicular gradients is $-1$"]
modelAnswer:
$m_{PQ}=\frac{7-2}{4+1}=1$. Perpendicular requires
$m_{RS}=\frac{10-k}{7-2}=-1$, giving $10-k=-5$ and $k=15$.

stem: Using slopes, prove that points $\mathrm{X}(0,-3), \mathrm{Y}(4,7)$ and $\mathrm{Z}(6,12)$ are collinear.
keyPoints: ["One common point plus equal gradients forces collinearity"]
modelAnswer:
$m_{XY}=\frac{7+3}{4-0}=\frac{5}{2}$ and $m_{YZ}=\frac{12-7}{6-4}=\frac{5}{2}$.
Equal gradients through the shared point Y mean all three points lie on one line: collinear.

stem: Find value of $y$ if points $P(4, y), Q(5,2)$ and $R(6,2 y+1)$ are collinear.
keyPoints: ["Shared segment slope keeps three points on one line"]
modelAnswer:
Collinearity needs $m_{PQ}=m_{QR}$:
$\frac{2-y}{5-4}=2-y$ and $\frac{(2y+1)-2}{6-5}=2y-1$.
So $2-y=2y-1$, giving $y=1$.

stem: Prove by using slopes that points $\mathrm{A}(3,-1), \mathrm{B}(-5,-5)$ and $\mathrm{C}(1,3)$ are vertices of a right angled triangle.
keyPoints: ["A product of gradients equal to $-1$ proves the right angle"]
modelAnswer:
$m_{AB}=\frac{-5+1}{-5-3}=\frac{1}{2}$, $m_{AC}=\frac{3+1}{1-3}=-2$.
Their product is $-1$, so AB meets AC at right angles at A:
triangle ABC is right angled.

stem: Using slope, prove that $\mathrm{A}(-2,1), \mathrm{B}(6,3), \mathrm{C}(10,5)$ and $\mathrm{D}(2,3)$ are vertices of parallelogram.
keyPoints: ["Show both pairs of opposite sides parallel"]
modelAnswer:
$m_{AB}=\frac{3-1}{6+2}=\frac{1}{4}$ and $m_{DC}=\frac{5-3}{10-2}=\frac{1}{4}$;
$|AB|=|DC|=\sqrt{68}$.
Also $m_{AD}=\frac{3-1}{2+2}=\frac{1}{2}$ and $m_{BC}=\frac{1}{2}$ with $|AD|=|BC|=\sqrt{20}$.
Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel and equal: parallelogram.

stem: $\mathrm{P}(x, y), \mathrm{Q}(-2,2), \mathrm{R}(1,4)$ and $\mathrm{S}(10,1)$ are vertices of a parallelogram. Find $\mathrm{P}(x, y)$.
keyPoints: ["Bisecting diagonals share one midpoint"]
modelAnswer:
Diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so midpoints of PR and QS coincide.
$\left(\frac{x+1}{2}, \frac{y+4}{2}\right)=\left(\frac{-2+10}{2}, \frac{2+1}{2}\right)=(4,1.5)$.
Hence $x=7$ and $y=-1$: $P=(7,-1)$.

stem: Three vertices of a rhombus are $\mathrm{A}(2,-1), \mathrm{B}(3,4)$ and $\mathrm{C}(-2,3)$. Find fourth vertex.
keyPoints: ["Rhombus diagonals share their midpoint","Verify the result against a second point or pair"]
modelAnswer:
A rhombus is a parallelogram, so its diagonals AC and BD bisect each other.
Midpoint AC: $\left(\frac{2-2}{2}, \frac{-1+3}{2}\right)=(0,1)$.
Setting midpoint BD equal: $\frac{3+x}{2}=0$ and $\frac{4+y}{2}=1$, giving $D=(-3,-2)$.

stem:
If $(5,0),(0,5)$ and $(8,8)$ are vertices of a triangle, find:
(i) slopes of sides.
(ii) slopes of medians.
(iii) slopes of altitudes.
keyPoints: ["Median targets the midpoint of the opposite side","Altitude slopes invert and negate the side slopes"]
modelAnswer:
Let A$(5,0)$, B$(0,5)$, C$(8,8)$.
i. Side slopes: $m_{AB}=\frac{5-0}{0-5}=-1$, $m_{BC}=\frac{8-5}{8-0}=\frac{3}{8}$, $m_{CA}=\frac{0-8}{5-8}=\frac{8}{3}$.
ii. Medians go to opposite-side midpoints $(4,\frac{13}{2})$, $(\frac{13}{2},4)$, $(\frac{5}{2},\frac{5}{2})$:
slopes $\frac{13/2}{-1}=-\frac{13}{2}$, $\frac{-1}{13/2}=-\frac{2}{13}$, and $1$ respectively.
iii. Altitudes are perpendicular to the sides: from A slope $\frac{8}{3}$? No, perpendicular to BC means $-\frac{8}{3}$;
from B perpendicular to CA: $-\frac{3}{8}$; from C perpendicular to AB: $1$.

stem:
Find equation of line in symmetric form when:
(i) $\left(x_{1}, y_{1}\right)=(-4,2)$ and $\tan \theta=\frac{3}{4}$
(ii) $\left(x_{1}, y_{1}\right)=(6,-6)$ and $\theta=30^{\circ}$
keyPoints: ["Symmetric form divides by direction cosines"]
modelAnswer:
Symmetric form: $\frac{x-x_{1}}{\cos\theta}=\frac{y-y_{1}}{\sin\theta}$.
i. With $\tan\theta=\frac{3}{4}$: $\cos\theta=\frac{4}{5}$, $\sin\theta=\frac{3}{5}$, so
$\frac{x+4}{4/5}=\frac{y-2}{3/5}$.
ii. $\theta=30^{\circ}$: $\cos\theta=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, $\sin\theta=\frac{1}{2}$, so
$\frac{x-6}{\sqrt{3}/2}=\frac{y+6}{1/2}$.

stem:
Find equation of line in normal form when:
(i) $p=5$ and $\theta=120^{\circ}$
(ii) $p=10$ and $\tan \theta=1$
keyPoints: ["p measures the perpendicular distance from the origin"]
modelAnswer:
Normal form: $x\cos\theta+y\sin\theta=p$, where $\theta$ is the angle of the normal.
i. $\cos120^{\circ}=-\frac{1}{2}$, $\sin120^{\circ}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$:
$-\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}y=5$, equivalently $-x+\sqrt{3}y=10$.
ii. $\tan\theta=1$ with acute normal angle: $\cos\theta=\sin\theta=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$:
$\frac{x+y}{\sqrt{2}}=10$, equivalently $x+y=10\sqrt{2}$.

stem:
Find the equation of straight line:
(i) through $(-4, -4)$ and parallel to the line with slope -5.
(ii) through $(5,-1)$ and perpendicular to the line with slope $\frac{1}{4}$.
(iii) having y-intercept $=4$ and parallel to the line with slope $\frac{1}{2}$.
(iv) having x-intercept $=-2$ and perpendicular to the line with slope $4$.
(v) through $(-1,4)$ and perpendicular to the line passing through $(3,0)$ and $(1,-2)$.
(vi) through $(6,-4)$ and parallel to the line passing through $(-5,2)$ and $(3,6)$.
keyPoints: ["Parallel copies the slope; perpendicular negates its reciprocal"]
modelAnswer:
i. Through $(-4,-4)$ with slope $-5$: $y+4=-5(x+4)$, i.e. $5x+y+24=0$.
ii. Through $(5,-1)$ perpendicular to slope $\frac{1}{2}$, so slope $=-2$:
$y+1=-2(x-5)$, i.e. $2x+y-9=0$.

stem: Find equation of the line through $(3,7)$ and parallel to the line $4 x-3 y+1=0$.
keyPoints: ["Read the slope from the general-form line first","Verify the result against a second point or pair"]

stem: Find equation of the line through $(-2,-1)$ and perpendicular to the line $x-2 y=0$.
keyPoints: ["Perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal"]
modelAnswer:
$x-2y=0$ has slope $\frac{1}{2}$; perpendicular slope $=-2$.
Through $(-2,-1)$: $y+1=-2(x+2)$, i.e. $2x+y+5=0$.

stem: Find equation of perpendicular bisector of line segment joining $(0,6)$ and $(2,-2)$.
keyPoints: ["Bisector combines the midpoint with the flipped slope"]
modelAnswer:
Segment joining $(0,6)$ and $(2,-2)$ has midpoint $(1,2)$
and slope $\frac{-2-6}{2-0}=-4$.
The perpendicular bisector passes through $(1,2)$ with slope $\frac{1}{4}$:
$y-2=\frac{1}{4}(x-1)$, i.e. $x-4y+7=0$.

stem:
Find equation of medians and altitudes of triangle with vertices
$$
A(0,4), B(4,6) \text { and } C(-2,-2).
$$
keyPoints: ["Altitude slopes are negative reciprocals of side slopes","Verify the result against a second point or pair"]
modelAnswer:
With A$(0,4)$, B$(4,6)$, C$(-2,-2)$:
Medians (to side midpoints $(1,2)$, $(-1,1)$, $(2,5)$):
from A: $y=-2x+4$; from B: slope $\frac{1-6}{-1-4}=1$, so $y=x+2$; from C: slope $\frac{5+2}{2+2}=\frac{7}{4}$, so $y+2=\frac{7}{4}(x+2)$.
Altitudes (perpendicular to sides $m_{BC}=\frac{4}{3}$, $m_{CA}=1$, $m_{AB}=\frac{1}{2}$):
from A: $y-4=-\frac{3}{4}x$, i.e. $3x+4y-16=0$; from B: $y-6=-(x-4)$, i.e. $x+y-10=0$;
from C: $y+2=-2(x+2)$, i.e. $2x+y+6=0$.

topicTitle: 8.3 Formula for the Gradient of a Line
stem:
Find the measure of angle from $l_{1}$ to $l_{2}$ if:
(i) slope of $l_{1}=0$ and slope of $l_{2}=1$
(ii) slope of $l_{1}=-0.5$ and slope of $l_{2}=4.5$
(iii) slope of $l_{1}=\tan 45^{\circ}$ and slope of $l_{2}=\tan 135^{\circ}$
keyPoints: ["Add $180^{\\circ}$ when the tangent comes out negative","Product $-1$ of slopes signals a right angle"]
modelAnswer:
Angle from $l_{1}$ to $l_{2}$ satisfies $\tan\alpha=\frac{m_{2}-m_{1}}{1+m_{1}m_{2}}$.
i. $\tan\alpha=\frac{1-0}{1+0}=1$, so $\alpha=45^{\circ}$.
ii. $\tan\alpha=\frac{4.5+0.5}{1-2.25}=\frac{5}{-1.25}=-4$; adding $180^{\circ}$ to the negative arctangent
gives $\alpha\approx104.04^{\circ}$.
iii. $m_{1}m_{2}=(1)(-1)=-1$: the lines are perpendicular, $\alpha=90^{\circ}$.

topicTitle: 8.3 Formula for the Gradient of a Line
keyPoints: ["Vertical sides shortcut straight to ninety degrees","Verify the result against a second point or pair"]
modelAnswer:
Compute both slopes, then use $\tan\alpha=\frac{m_{2}-m_{1}}{1+m_{1}m_{2}}$.
i. $m_{1}=0$, $l_{2}$ vertical: $\alpha=90^{\circ}$.
ii. $m_{1}=\frac{3}{5}$, $m_{2}=1$: $\tan\alpha=\frac{2/5}{8/5}=\frac{1}{4}$, $\alpha\approx14.04^{\circ}$.
iii. $m_{1}=\frac{1}{2}$, $m_{2}=1$: $\tan\alpha=\frac{1/2}{3/2}=\frac{1}{3}$, $\alpha\approx18.43^{\circ}$.
iv. $m_{1}=-1$, $m_{2}=0$: $\tan\alpha=1$, $\alpha=45^{\circ}$.
v. $m_{1}=-\frac{6}{7}$, $m_{2}=1$: $\tan\alpha=\frac{13/7}{1/7}=13$, $\alpha\approx85.60^{\circ}$.

topicTitle: 8.3 Formula for the Gradient of a Line
stem:
Find the interior angles of triangle ABC when:
(i) Slope of $\mathrm{AB}=0$, Slope of $\mathrm{BC}=-1$, Slope of $\mathrm{AC}=1$
(ii) Slope of $\mathrm{AB}=0.25$, Slope of $\mathrm{BC}=1.25$, Slope of $\mathrm{AC}=1$
(iii) Slope of $\mathrm{AB}=0.4$, Slope of $\mathrm{BC}=-1.5$, Slope of $\mathrm{AC}=1.667$
(iv) Slope of $\mathrm{AB}=-1$, Slope of $\mathrm{BC}=0.8$, Slope of $\mathrm{AC}=0$
keyPoints: ["Interior versus exterior choice must make the angles sum to one eighty","Verify the result against a second point or pair"]
modelAnswer:
Interior angles come from the pairwise tangent formula, choosing supplements where needed.
i. Sides $0,-1,1$: the $0$ and $-1$ sides meet the slope-$1$ side perpendicularly at C,
so $C=90^{\circ}$, $A=B=45^{\circ}$.
ii. $m_{AB}=0.25$, $m_{BC}=1.25$, $m_{AC}=1$:
$A=\tan^{-1}\left|\frac{1-0.25}{1+0.25}\right|=30.96^{\circ}$,
$B=\tan^{-1}\left|\frac{1.25-0.25}{1+0.3125}\right|=37.30^{\circ}$, $C=111.74^{\circ}$.
iii. $m_{AB}=0.4$, $m_{BC}=-1.5$, $m_{AC}=\frac{5}{3}$:
$A=\tan^{-1}\left|\frac{5/3-0.4}{1+(5/3)(0.4)}\right|=37.23^{\circ}$,
$B=\tan^{-1}\left|\frac{-1.5-0.4}{1-0.6}\right|=78.11^{\circ}$, $C=64.66^{\circ}$.
iv. $m_{AB}=-1$, $m_{BC}=0.8$, $m_{AC}=0$:
$A=45^{\circ}$, $C=\tan^{-1}(0.8)=38.66^{\circ}$, $B=96.34^{\circ}$.

topicTitle: 8.3 Formula for the Gradient of a Line
stem:
Find angle between lines:
(i) $3 x+2 y+5=0$ and $2 x-3 y+8=0$
(ii) $x+2 y-6=0$ and $2 x-4 y+9=0$
(iii) $6 x-y+1=0$ and $x-7 y+12=0$
keyPoints: ["General form lines convert via slope $=-a/b$","Verify the result against a second point or pair"]
modelAnswer:
Convert each line to slope form, then apply the angle formula.
i. Slopes $-\frac{3}{2}$ and $\frac{2}{3}$ multiply to $-1$: angle $90^{\circ}$.
ii. Slopes $-\frac{1}{2}$ and $\frac{1}{2}$: $\tan\theta=\frac{1}{3/4}=\frac{4}{3}$, $\theta\approx53.13^{\circ}$.
iii. Slopes $6$ and $\frac{1}{7}$: $\tan\theta=\left|\frac{1/7-6}{1+6/7}\right|=\frac{41}{13}$, $\theta\approx72.41^{\circ}$.

topicTitle: 8.3 Formula for the Gradient of a Line
stem:
Find the interior angles of triangle XYZ whose vertices are:
(i) $\mathrm{X}(-2,3), \mathrm{Y}(-3,-4), \mathrm{Z}(5,2)$
(ii) $\mathrm{X}(-3,2), \mathrm{Y}(0,-1), \mathrm{Z}(3,3)$
(iii) $\mathrm{X}(-2,0), \mathrm{Y}(1,-4), \mathrm{Z}(6,6)$
(iv) $\mathrm{X}(-4,1), \mathrm{Y}(0,-3), \mathrm{Z}(4,3)$
keyPoints: ["Right-angle detection shortens the work considerably","Verify the result against a second point or pair"]
modelAnswer:
i. Slopes: $XY=7$, $YZ=\frac{3}{4}$, $ZX=-\frac{1}{7}$; $XY \perp ZX$, so $X=90^{\circ}$,
and $Y=Z=45^{\circ}$.
ii. $XY=-1$, $YZ=\frac{4}{3}$, $ZX=\frac{1}{6}$:
$Y=180^{\circ}-\tan^{-1}(7)\approx98.13^{\circ}$, $X\approx54.46^{\circ}$, $Z\approx27.41^{\circ}$.
iii. $XY=-\frac{4}{3}$, $YZ=2$, $ZX=\frac{3}{4}$; product $XY\cdot ZX=-1$, so $X=90^{\circ}$,
$Y\approx63.43^{\circ}$, $Z\approx26.57^{\circ}$.
iv. $XY=-1$, $YZ=1.5$, $ZX=\frac{1}{4}$: $X\approx59.04^{\circ}$, $Y\approx78.69^{\circ}$, $Z\approx42.27^{\circ}$.

topicTitle: 8.3 Formula for the Gradient of a Line
stem:
Find the point of intersection of lines:
(i) $2 x+y+1=0$ and $x-y-4=0$
(ii) $x+y+3=0$ and $2 x-5 y+8=0$
(iii) $2 x+5 y+3=0$ and $3 x-4 y-5=0$
keyPoints: ["Substitution or elimination both reach the crossing point"]
modelAnswer:
Solve each pair simultaneously.
i. From $x-y-4=0$, $y=x-4$; substituting into $2x+y+1=0$ gives $x=1$, $y=-3$.
ii. $y=-x-3$ into $2x-5y+8=0$ gives $7x+23=0$: point $\left(-\frac{23}{7}, \frac{2}{7}\right)$.
iii. Eliminating $y$ (first $\times4$, second $\times5$, add): $23x-13=0$, so $x=\frac{13}{23}$
and $y=-\frac{19}{23}$.

topicTitle: 8.3 Formula for the Gradient of a Line
stem:
Find equation of line passing through point of intersection of lines $3 x+2 y+1=0, x-2 y+3=0$ and
(a) passing through point $(-1,0)$.
(b) parallel to $3 x-4 y+3=0$.
keyPoints: ["Family lines pass through the computed intersection","Verify the result against a second point or pair"]
modelAnswer:

topicTitle: 8.3 Formula for the Gradient of a Line

(b) parallel to $y$-axis.

modelAnswer:

and $x=-\frac{9}{22}$.
(a) Parallel to the x-axis: $y=\frac{7}{11}$.
(b) Parallel to the y-axis: $x=-\frac{9}{22}$.

topicTitle: 8.3 Formula for the Gradient of a Line
stem:
Find equation of line passing through point of intersection of lines $2 x-y+2=0, x-2 y+1=0$ and
(a) parallel to $x-2 y+11=0$
(b) perpendicular to $2 x+5 y+2=0$.
keyPoints: ["General-form slopes read as $-a/b$","Verify the result against a second point or pair"]
modelAnswer:
Subtracting twice the second equation from the first: $3y=0$, so $y=0$ and $x=-1$.
Intersection: $(-1,0)$.
(a) Parallel to $x-2y+11=0$ (slope $\frac{1}{2}$): $y=\frac{1}{2}(x+1)$, i.e. $x-2y+1=0$.
(b) Perpendicular to $2x+5y+2=0$ (slope $-\frac{2}{5}$), so slope $\frac{5}{2}$:
$y=\frac{5}{2}(x+1)$, i.e. $5x-2y+5=0$.

topicTitle: 8.3 Formula for the Gradient of a Line
stem:
Find equation of line passing through point of intersection of lines $x-2 y+4=0,3 x-y-3=0$ and
(a) parallel to line passing through $(2,-3)$ and $(0,4)$.
(b) perpendicular to line passing through $(2,-3)$ and $(0,4)$.
keyPoints: ["Reference-line slopes transfer with sign flips for perpendiculars","Verify the result against a second point or pair"]
modelAnswer:
From $3x-y-3=0$, $y=3x-3$; substituting into $x-2y+4=0$ gives $-5x+10=0$,
so the intersection is $(2,3)$.
The reference line through $(2,-3)$ and $(0,4)$ has slope $-\frac{7}{2}$.
(a) Parallel through $(2,3)$: $y-3=-\frac{7}{2}(x-2)$, i.e. $7x+2y-20=0$.
(b) Perpendicular through $(2,3)$: slope $\frac{2}{7}$: $y-3=\frac{2}{7}(x-2)$,
i.e. $2x-7y+17=0$ (completing the truncated printed part (b)).
